variables.title: Variables
variables.definition: Variables are containers that store data values for reuse and manipulation in a program.
variables.whyUse: They allow you to store and manage data dynamically instead of hardcoding values.
variables.whenUse: Whenever you need to store data temporarily, like user inputs, API responses, or counters.
variables.thinking: Think of variables as labeled boxes where you can store and retrieve values. Decide whether the value will change ('let') or stay constant ('const').

easy: Declare a variable 'username' and store your name. Print it.
Create a constant 'PI' and assign 3.141. Try reassigning it to see the error.
Declare variables 'a=10' and 'b=20'. Print their sum.
Declare a variable without assigning a value and print it.
Change the value of a variable twice and print the final result.
medium: Swap values of variables a=5 and b=10 without using a temporary variable.
Declare multiple variables in one statement: x=1, y=2, z=3 and print them.
Demonstrate variable hoisting with 'var' using console.log before declaration.
Show how scope works by declaring 'let' inside a block and trying to access it outside.
Explain why reassigning a constant variable gives an error.
hard: Create a counter variable that counts how many times a function is called.
Store a user's profile (name, age, email) in variables and print a formatted profile card.
Show difference in block scope using 'var' vs 'let' inside an if statement.
Implement a simple bank balance tracker with deposit and withdrawal variables.
Write a program that swaps three variables in a circular manner (a→b, b→c, c→a).

data-types.title: Data Types
data-types.definition: Data types define the kind of values a variable can hold, like numbers, strings, or objects.
data-types.whyUse: They help determine what operations can be performed on the data.
data-types.whenUse: Whenever you declare a variable, you are working with a data type.
confusions: Arrays and objects are reference types
data-types.thinking: Think of data types as categories of information. Always check the type with 'typeof' to avoid bugs.

easy: Check the type of: 'hello', 42, true, null, undefined.
Convert string '123' into a number and number 456 into a string.
Create an array with mixed data types and print each element's type.
Check if a boolean variable is true or false using typeof.
Store today's date using Date object and check its type.
medium: Create an object with properties of different types (string, number, boolean).
Compare null and undefined using == and ===.
Demonstrate NaN by dividing a string by a number.
Check typeof NaN and explain why it's 'number'.
Show that arrays and objects are reference types with an example.
hard: Write a function that takes any input and returns its type.
Check if a variable is an array using Array.isArray().
Create a nested object with different data types and print all values recursively.
Implement a type-checking utility function that distinguishes arrays, objects, null, and dates.
Write a function that safely parses JSON and returns its type.

operators.title: Operators
operators.definition: Operators are symbols used to perform operations on values and variables.
operators.whyUse: They allow you to perform calculations, comparisons, and logic building.
operators.whenUse: When doing arithmetic, decision-making, or updating values.
operators.thinking: Think of operators as verbs in sentences. They define how values interact with each other.

easy: Calculate: 10 + 5 * 2 - 8 / 4.
Check if 5 == '5' and 5 === '5'.
Use += to increment a variable from 0 to 10.
Use modulus operator (%) to find remainder of 17 divided by 5.
Check if a number is greater than or equal to another number.
medium: Write a ternary operator to check if a number is even or odd.
Check if a number is between 10 and 20 using comparison operators.
Use && and || to combine conditions in an if statement.
Demonstrate operator precedence with a complex expression.
Show an example where using '=' instead of '==' creates a bug.
hard: Write a calculator function that takes two numbers and an operator (+, -, *, /) and returns the result.
Use ! operator to invert a boolean and explain double negation (!!).
Combine arithmetic and assignment operators to calculate compound interest.
Write a program that simulates exponentiation without using ** operator.
Use bitwise operators (&, |, ^) to solve a small problem.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.definition: Conditionals let you run different code based on conditions being true or false.
conditionals.whyUse: They allow programs to make decisions and follow different paths.
conditionals.whenUse: When you want to handle multiple possible outcomes.
conditionals.thinking: Think of conditionals like crossroads. You choose the path depending on the condition.

easy: Write an if statement to check if a number is positive or negative.
Write a ternary operator to return 'adult' if age >= 18, 'minor' otherwise.
Check if a variable exists and is not null using truthy checks.
Write an if statement that checks if a number is divisible by 3.
Use if-else to check if a string is empty or not.
medium: Use switch case to handle different string commands: 'start', 'stop', 'pause'.
Create nested if statements to check grade ranges (A, B, C, D, F).
Write conditionals to validate user input (non-empty string, valid email format).
Write a program that checks if a year is a leap year.
Use conditionals to decide shipping cost based on purchase amount.
hard: Create a grading system with multiple else-if statements and real scores.
Write a program that takes weather input ('rainy', 'sunny', 'snowy') and prints what to wear.
Use short-circuit evaluation with || to provide default values when user input is missing.
Implement a login check with username and password validation using conditionals.
Write a program that selects a discount rate based on customer type and purchase amount.

loops.title: Loops
loops.definition: Loops are used to repeat code multiple times until a condition is met.
loops.whyUse: They make repetitive tasks easier and reduce code duplication.
loops.whenUse: When processing arrays, repeating tasks, or waiting for conditions.
confusions: Infinite loops when forgetting to update condition
loops.thinking: Think of loops as automatic machines that repeat tasks until told to stop.

easy: Write a for loop to print numbers 1 to 10.
Use while loop to sum numbers until total exceeds 100.
Use do-while loop to ask user for input at least once.
Write a for loop to print each character of a string.
Print first 10 even numbers using a loop.
medium: Iterate through an array of names and print each in uppercase.
Print multiplication table of 5 using a loop.
Use continue to skip odd numbers and print only even numbers between 1-20.
Write a loop that calculates factorial of 6.
Use a loop to reverse a string.
hard: Create nested loops to print a 5x5 star pattern.
Write a loop that finds prime numbers between 1 and 100.
Use for...in loop to iterate through object properties and print key-value pairs.
Use nested loops to generate a multiplication table up to 10x10.
Write a loop that checks for palindrome strings in an array.

functions.title: Functions
functions.definition: Functions are reusable blocks of code that perform specific tasks.
functions.whyUse: They avoid repetition, improve readability, and enable modular programming.
functions.whenUse: Whenever you need to reuse logic multiple times or isolate functionality.
confusions: Difference between function declaration and expression
Arrow function vs normal function (this binding)
functions.thinking: Think of functions like recipes. They take ingredients (parameters) and return results.

easy: Write a function that takes two numbers and returns their sum.
Create an arrow function that squares a number.
Write a function with default parameter values.
Write a function that prints 'Hello, JavaScript!'.
Write a function that returns the length of a string.
medium: Write a recursive function to calculate factorial of a number.
Use rest parameters to create a function that sums any number of arguments.
Create a function that takes a callback and executes it.
Write a function that returns the maximum of three numbers.
Write a function that reverses a given string.
hard: Create a closure function that remembers how many times it's called.
Write a higher-order function that takes an array and a function, applies the function to each element.
Write an IIFE that prints 'Hello, World!' immediately.
Write a function that returns another function to multiply a number by a given factor.
Implement memoization for a Fibonacci function.

arrays.title: Arrays
arrays.definition: Arrays are ordered collections of elements stored in a single variable.
arrays.whyUse: They allow you to store and manage multiple values in one structure.
arrays.whenUse: When you want to group related values like a list of names or numbers.
confusions: Difference between push, pop, shift, unshift
arrays.thinking: Think of arrays like a train with numbered seats. Each seat holds a value you can access by index.

easy: Create an array of 5 fruits and print them.
Access the first and last element of an array.
Add and remove elements using push and pop.
Find the length of an array.
Replace an element at index 2 with a new value.
medium: Loop through an array and print each element in uppercase.
Use map to square each number in an array.
Find the largest number in an array.
Filter out numbers greater than 50 from an array.
Join array elements into a single string.
hard: Flatten a nested array [[1,2],[3,4]] into [1,2,3,4].
Remove duplicate values from an array.
Write a function to reverse an array without using reverse().
Sort an array of strings alphabetically.
Find intersection of two arrays.

objects.title: Objects
objects.definition: Objects are collections of key-value pairs used to store structured data.
objects.whyUse: They allow grouping of related data and methods together.
objects.whenUse: When modeling entities like users, products, or configurations.
confusions: Difference between shallow and deep copy
objects.thinking: Think of objects as dictionaries where keys are words and values are their meanings.

easy: Create an object for a car with properties: brand, model, year.
Access and print a property value using dot notation.
Add a new property 'color' to the object.
Update a property value in an object.
Print all keys of an object.
medium: Loop through an object and print all keys and values.
Delete a property from an object.
Check if a property exists in an object.
Create an object with a method and call it.
Use Object.keys() and Object.values() to print all keys and values.
hard: Create a nested object for a user with address details.
Clone an object without reference issues.
Write a function that merges two objects.
Deep copy an object using JSON methods.
Write a function to compare two objects for equality.

events.title: Events
events.definition: Events are actions or occurrences that happen in the browser, like clicks or key presses.
events.whyUse: They let your program respond to user interactions.
events.thinking: Think of events like signals. When something happens, your code listens and reacts.

easy: Add a click event listener to a button that prints 'Button clicked!'.
Create an input field and log its value on change.
Show an alert when a page loads.
Print a message when the mouse enters a div.
Log a message when a key is released.
medium: Prevent a form from submitting using event.preventDefault().
Add mouseover event to change background color of a div.
Track keydown events and print which key was pressed.
Add a double-click event to toggle text size.
Use event.target to print clicked element's tag.
hard: Implement event delegation for a list of items.
Create a custom event and dispatch it.
Build a simple counter with increment/decrement buttons using events.
Stop event propagation in nested elements and explain the effect.
Implement drag and drop for an element.

dom.title: DOM
dom.definition: DOM (Document Object Model) represents the structure of a webpage as a tree of objects.
dom.whyUse: It allows JavaScript to interact with and manipulate webpage content.
dom.whenUse: When dynamically updating HTML, CSS, or responding to user actions.
dom.thinking: Think of the DOM like a family tree where each node is connected and can be accessed or modified.

easy: Select a paragraph by ID and change its text.
Change the background color of a div using JavaScript.
Add a new list item to an unordered list.
Change the src attribute of an image.
Hide and show an element using style.display.
medium: Select all paragraphs and change their font size.
Create a new element dynamically and append it to the body.
Remove an element from the DOM.
Add a CSS class dynamically to an element.
Replace an existing element with a new one.
hard: Build a simple to-do list app with add and delete functionality.
Traverse the DOM tree to find parent and child nodes.
Implement a light/dark mode toggle using DOM manipulation.
Build a modal popup using DOM methods.
Create a live character counter for a textarea.
